intro.text: General Description of Business. Arcosa, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries (“Arcosa,” “Company,” “we,” or “our”), headquartered in Dallas, Texas, is a provider of infrastructure-related products and solutions with leading brands serving construction, engineered structures, and transportation markets in North America. Arcosa is a Delaware corporation and was incorporated in 2018. Our individual businesses have built reputations for quality, service, and operational excellence over decades. Arcosa serves a broad spectrum of infrastructure-related markets and is strategically focused on driving organic and disciplined acquisition growth to capitalize on the fragmented nature of many of the industries in which we operate.

Our primary sources of liquidity include cash flow from operations, our existing cash balance, availability under the revolving credit facility, and, as necessary, the issuance of additional long-term debt or equity. We may also consider undertaking disciplined acquisitions, organic investment projects, additional return of capital to stockholders, or funding other general corporate purposes to the extent we have available liquidity.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The provision for income taxes for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023 was $32.9 million, $36.3 million, and $36.7 million, respectively. The effective tax rate for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023 was 13.6%, 27.9%, and 18.7%, respectively. The change in the effective tax rate for the year ended December 31, 2025 is primarily due to lower state income taxes, higher AMP tax credits, and lower foreign taxes.

Our effective tax rate differs from the federal tax rate of 21.0% due to AMP tax credits, state income taxes, statutory depletion deductions, compensation-related items, and other foreign adjustments. For a reconciliation of the federal tax rate to our effective tax rate, see Note 9. "Income Taxes" to the Consolidated Financial Statements.

See Note 9. "Income Taxes" to the Consolidated Financial Statements for a further discussion of income taxes.

lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Engineered Structures segment, constituted 12.2%, 10.8%, and 8.1% of consolidated revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
GE Vernova accounted for approximately 12.2% of our consolidated revenues in 2025 up from 10.8% of consolidated revenues in 2024.

Revenues from one customer included in the Engineered Structures segment constituted 12.2 %, 10.8 %, and 8.1 % of consolidated revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
Arcosa depends on its key management employees, and Arcosa may not be able to retain their services in the future.
Arcosa’s success depends on the continued services of its executive team and key management employees, none of whom currently have an employment agreement with Arcosa.
Arcosa depends on professional labor across its businesses and skilled labor in the manufacture, maintenance, and repair of Arcosa’s products.
In some instances, Arcosa relies on a limited number of suppliers for certain raw materials, parts, and components needed in its production.

Arcosa owns and operates manufacturing and mining facilities of various ages and levels of automated control and relies on a number of third parties as part of Arcosa’s supply chain, including for the efficient distribution of products to Arcosa’s customers.

Arcosa's operations partially depend on Arcosa's ability to obtain timely deliveries of raw materials, parts, and components in acceptable quantities and quality from Arcosa's domestic and foreign suppliers.
A significant portion of Arcosa’s business depends on the adequate supply of raw materials and numerous specialty and other parts and components at competitive prices.

The success and viability of these operations depend on the accuracy of Arcosa’s reserve estimates, the costs of production and the ability to economically distribute the natural aggregates and specialty materials.

In addition, Arcosa's success in recovering natural aggregates and specialty materials depends on the ability to maintain permits for existing mines and secure and permit new reserve locations in areas that make distribution of materials economically viable.
The success and viability of Arcosa's recycled aggregates operation depends on Arcosa's success in procuring supply stock for processing recycled materials into recycled aggregates.

The extent to which a pandemic, epidemic, or other public health emergency, as well as government shutdowns related thereto or otherwise, could impact our business will depend on numerous evolving factors that we may not be able to accurately predict.
In general, Arcosa may rely upon banks and capital markets to fund its growth strategy.

Likewise, if Arcosa's suppliers face challenges obtaining credit, selling their products to customers that require purchasing credit, or otherwise operating their businesses, the supply of materials Arcosa purchases from them to manufacture its products may be interrupted.
Arcosa produces certain products at its manufacturing facilities in Mexico and relies on cross-border supply chains.

Arcosa and its customers depend on government spending, funding and routine operations from federal, state and local government agencies, and any disruption in government funding or other functions could harm Arcosa's business.
Furthermore, certain of Arcosa’s businesses depend on government spending for infrastructure and other similar building activities, including Stavola's business activities in New Jersey.

Furthermore, Arcosa relies on government personnel to conduct certain routine business processes for the inspection and delivery of certain products that, if disrupted, could have an impact on Arcosa's revenues and business.

For example, our barge business depends on services provided by the U.S. Coast Guard and a government shutdown may limit the Coast Guard's ability to conduct such services, which could impair our ability to deliver vessels on schedule, increase logistical and compliance costs, and disrupt customer operations.

Arcosa relies on information technology infrastructure and architecture, including hardware, cloud computing networks, software, people, and processes to manage protected, confidential, and other sensitive information to conduct Arcosa’s business in the ordinary course.
These tools depend on data quality, model design, human oversight, and third-party software and services.
Arcosa relies on patent, copyright, and trademark law, and trade secret protection and confidentiality and/or license agreements with others to protect Arcosa’s intellectual property rights.

Our primary sources of liquidity include cash flow from operations, our existing cash balance, availability under the revolving credit facility, and, as necessary, the issuance of additional long-term debt or equity.
